results.controlIntent: a. Use internal system clocks to produce time stamps for audit records; and b. Record, for audit records, time stamps meeting [Assignment: organization-defined granularity of time measurement] that use Coordinated Universal Time, have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time, or that include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

judgment.rationale: The two CloudTrail audit records retrieved for the churn-predictor-endpoint (CreateEndpoint and UpdateEndpoint) both carry timestamps in ISO 8601 format with the 'Z' (UTC) suffix (e.g., "2025-12-01T11:00:00Z", "2026-03-15T14:22:00Z"). This satisfies AU-8.v3(a) — timestamps are produced by AWS CloudTrail's internal system clock — and AU-8.v3(b) — timestamps use Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), indicated by the 'Z' designator, with second-level granularity (HH:MM:SS). Second-level granularity is substantively adequate for most organization-defined requirements. The change-control anomalies noted in the event metadata (deployment before registry approval, missing registry entry) are relevant to other controls (e.g., CM-3, SA-10) and do not affect AU-8 conformance. Confidence is medium rather than high because no organization-defined granularity policy document was available to confirm the required precision level, and only two audit events were sampled.
gaps: No organization-defined granularity policy document was available to confirm the required time measurement precision (e.g., millisecond vs. second) — human attestation or policy retrieval needed.
Only two CloudTrail events were sampled; a broader audit log review would increase confidence that all event types consistently use UTC timestamps.
No evidence of NTP/time-sync configuration for underlying compute resources was available to confirm use of authoritative internal system clocks.
